*Table: Reported laboratory and SDL end-effectors are predominantly workflow-specific, while grasp success, endurance, and MTBI are usually absent. The strongest quantitative evidence comes from controlled component studies rather than sustained SDL deployment.*

| Rank | Project title | Specific publishable claim | Key measurements required | Baseline to beat | Most likely failure mode | De-risked by CADSmith? | Realistic venue | Timeline |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Closed-loop generative end-effector design for materials labware | An object/specification-to-CadQuery-to-FDM-to-robot-test loop can generate application-specific fingers that outperform human-designed universal and object-specific fingers across vials, SEM stubs, well plates, and coupons. This extends Fit2Form beyond geometry-only optimization and current text-to-CAD beyond geometric similarity (pqac-00000029, pqac-00000030, pqac-00000008). | Execution and printability rate; human intervention and design time; mass; retention force; success under randomized translational and angular offsets; empty-versus-filled vial performance; seating success; damage; at least 1,000 cycles per finalist; ablations of kernel checks, VLM judging, and physical feedback. | Expert-designed rigid fingers; Zwirnmann-style compliant fingers, whose microtube top-grasp wrest force improved from 5.0(5) to 14.9(22) N; imprint fingers; zero-shot CADSmith; optionally Fit2Form-style generated fingers (pqac-00000002, pqac-00000034). | Chamfer distance and render quality do not predict contact mechanics; FDM tolerances, friction, anisotropy, or pose errors erase the predicted advantage. | **Strongly.** Existing CadQuery generation, OpenCASCADE measurements, render judging, refinement, and benchmark infrastructure cover most of the digital pipeline. | *Additive Manufacturing*; *IEEE RA-L*; *Digital Discovery* | 9–18 months |
| 2 | Compliance-versus-precision map for low-cost laboratory manipulation | Passive finger and fixture compliance can convert a hobby-class arm’s pose-error distribution into reliable vial insertion, crucible placement, and coupon seating, but only within a measured capture envelope. Existing laboratory fingers demonstrate displacement tolerance without quantifying this system-level substitution (pqac-00000001, pqac-00000002). | Independently impose lateral, axial, and angular errors; map success probability and peak force versus clearance; compare rigid chamfer, TPU pad, flexure, Fin-Ray-like finger, and RCC; measure seating error, cycle time, damage, and 1,000–10,000 cycles. | Rigid parallel fingers and fixtures; visual correction alone; literature-inspired compliant fingers tested at 20 N pinch and 100 N power-grasp conditions (pqac-00000002). | Compliance reduces force but permits tilt, false seating, or poor final pose; printed flexures creep or fatigue. | **Moderately.** CADSmith can generate controlled variants and fixtures; force instrumentation and mechanism models are new. | *IEEE RA-L*; *Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing*; *Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics* | 6–12 months |
| 3 | End-effector reliability benchmark for low-cost SDL arms | A sub-$5k arm with task-specific FDM tooling can reach a defensible operation-level reliability target on a multi-object materials-SDL benchmark while exposing MTBI, recovery rate, and failure taxonomy that deployed SDL papers omit. Existing reports emphasize throughput without handling-failure denominators (pqac-00000050, pqac-00000052). | Thousands of pick, place, and seat operations; per-object success; MTBF/MTBI; retries and autonomous recovery; slip, collision, false-grasp, mis-seat, tool-change, and contamination failures; thermal drift; payload and CG effects; confidence intervals; intervention minutes per 100 operations. | Stock PiPER gripper; expert-designed custom gripper; established implied 97.5% per-sample context; MATTERIX’s 75% real pick-and-place and 90% pouring as digital-twin comparators, not deployment targets (pqac-00000020). | Hidden thermal, backlash, communication, or current-control limitations dominate and cannot be repaired by finger geometry. | **Indirectly.** CADSmith accelerates tooling; the main contribution is metrology, logging, statistics, and recovery software. | *HardwareX* plus dataset; *Digital Discovery*; *IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine* | 6–12 months |
| 4 | Lightweight printed kinematic tool changer for a 1.5 kg arm | A predominantly FDM magnetic Maxwell/Kelvin coupler can provide low mass, passive docking, service pass-throughs, and tool-center-point repeatability adequate for labware handling without consuming an industrial changer’s payload fraction. Precision metal couplings achieve approximately 0.3–1.4 µm three-sigma repeatability, but wear can degrade steel contacts toward 10 µm after hundreds of cycles (pqac-00000024, pqac-00000026). | Changer mass; six-degree-of-freedom redocking repeatability over at least 1,000 cycles; preload; pull-off force; torsional stiffness; TCP shift under payload; capture range; wear and debris sensitivity; failed docks; electrical resistance; robot-task success before and after changes. | Bolted manual replacement; dowel-pin printed coupler; magnetic faceplate; commercial lightweight changer if available. Compare against ±5 µm split-groove and 0.3–1.4 µm precision-coupling results only as aspirational references (pqac-00000026). | Printed grooves wear, creep, embed powder, or lack stiffness; magnets collect ferromagnetic powder. | **Strongly for geometry; weakly for tribology.** Durable contact inserts and wear characterization are new. | *HardwareX*; *Precision Engineering*; *Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics* | 6–10 months |
| 5 | Robotic DSC-crucible and press-fit-lid station | A low-cost arm plus passive centering nest, guided punch, and inexpensive load sensing can place thin aluminum crucibles and lids and complete press-fitting with controlled force and high verified seating success. The scan found no quantitative robotic DSC press-fit study; related crucible work chose screw-on rather than press-fit lids. | Crucible and lid dimensional distributions; force–displacement curves; peak and seating force; misalignment capture envelope; lid deformation, leaks, or mass loss; visual or height verification; DSC blank effects; 500–1,000 closures; jam and double-lid recovery. | Manual pressing; rigid robot-only pressing; manually operated commercial DSC press; passive nest without compliance or force sensing. | Thin lids buckle, stick together, or appear seated while leaking; required force exceeds safe PiPER contact capability. | **Moderately.** CADSmith can generate nests, singulators, punches, and compliance variants; analytical and force validation are new. | *HardwareX*; *Thermochimica Acta*; *Digital Discovery* | 6–12 months |
| 6 | Fixed-focus wrist vision for last-centimeter laboratory servoing | A calibrated Raspberry Pi HQ fixed-focus eye-in-hand camera with fiducial or geometric servoing can compensate for low-cost-arm error during the final 50–200 mm and improve grasp and seating reliability without autofocus-induced intrinsics drift. Published low-cost systems report 90% grasping with ±3 mm residual error and edge-of-field errors above 5 mm (pqac-00000040, pqac-00000042). | Intrinsics and hand–eye stability versus time and temperature; depth of field at 50, 100, 150, and 200 mm; occlusion maps; terminal pose error; open-loop versus one-shot versus continuous servoing; latency; lighting sensitivity; recovery rate. | Teach-and-repeat; overhead camera; wrist camera without final servoing; autofocus module; compliance-only insertion. | Jaws or objects occlude the target when correction matters; monocular scale ambiguity and vibration dominate. | **Moderately.** CADSmith can optimize brackets, fiducial visibility, and occlusion-aware finger geometry; vision and control are new. | *IEEE RA-L*; *Sensors*; *Robotics*; *Digital Discovery* | 4–9 months |
| 7 | Open powder scoop with quantified decontamination | A passive or cam-actuated replaceable FDM scoop can transfer cohesive AlSi10Mg and Si with competitive dose repeatability while a measured cleaning or disposable-tool protocol bounds carryover. MATTERIX represents powder as particles and demonstrates virtual weighing and scooping, but cohesive behavior is unvalidated (pqac-00000016, pqac-00000018, pqac-00000021). | Delivered-mass bias and CV; residual mass; aerosol or spillage loss; triboelectric charge; humidity dependence; adhesion by material and surface treatment; tracer, ICP/OES, or XRF carryover; cleaning efficacy and time; 100–500 doses per condition. | Manual spatula; in-house `powder-doser`; simple printed scoop; MATTERIX/Isaac prediction; disposable versus brushed, vacuumed, or solvent-cleaned tools. | Cohesion and electrostatics overwhelm geometry; cleaning redistributes contamination; aluminum-dust safety restricts testing. | **Moderately.** CADSmith can generate scoop families and disposable liners; powder metrology, electrostatics, safety, and decontamination validation are new. | *Powder Technology*; *HardwareX*; *Digital Discovery* | 9–18 months |


*Table: Seven projects are ranked by novelty, feasibility, evidentiary burden, and fit with the existing PiPER, FDM, and CADSmith capabilities. The highest-value opportunity is a physically closed generative-design loop, while reliability benchmarking offers the fastest defensible systems contribution.*
artifact-02:
| Approach / system | What it does | Key metric / result | Fabricated and tested? | Relevance to end-effector design | Gap vs. CADSmith |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fit2Form** — Ha, Agrawal & Song (2020) | Generates object-specific parallel-jaw finger geometry from target-object shape using TSDF generation and a learned fitness model for grasp success, stability, and robustness. | Physical protocol: 5 N grasp, 15 cm lift, X/Y shaking, ≈30 N poke, and rotational perturbations; four simulation-discovered grasp strategies also appeared physically. No aggregate success rate or endurance result was reported in the retrieved evidence. (pqac-00000006, pqac-00000029, pqac-00000034) | **Yes, partially closed loop:** generated fingers were printed, mounted on a WSG50, and tested on printed objects. | Closest established precedent for object geometry → generated finger form → fabrication → physical grasp evaluation. | Does not generate conventional editable parametric CAD, optimize material/strength/kinematics/controller, use physical results for iterative redesign, or demonstrate laboratory objects and an SDL arm. CADSmith supplies editable CadQuery, exact-kernel validation, and iterative VLM feedback, but not yet contact-aware or physical feedback. |
| **Co-Design of Soft Gripper with Neural Physics** — Yi et al. (2025) | Jointly optimizes block-wise finger stiffness and grasp pose using a differentiable neural surrogate trained on tendon/flexure simulations. | Optimized printed grippers reportedly outperformed rigid, overly compliant, and other baseline designs in simulation and hardware; the retrieved evidence does not provide a single aggregate percentage. (pqac-00000030) | **Yes:** structural variants were printed and physically evaluated. | Demonstrates credible morphology–grasp-pose co-design and hardware validation. | Uses a predefined flexure-finger family rather than open-ended labware-to-CadQuery synthesis; fabrication is not an autonomous design-test-redesign loop. CADSmith is broader geometrically but presently lacks its mechanics-aware objective. |
| **IterCAD** — Hu et al. (2026) | Iteratively debugs and refines CadQuery using execution, visual/geometric feedback, supervised tuning, geometry-aware reinforcement learning, and viable-prefix masking. | Text2CAD: **0.64% invalid**, mean Chamfer Distance **10.92**, median **0.10**; CADPrompt: **2% invalid**, mean **10.45**, median **2.42**. Limited to single parts, with occasional hard-coded and poorly maintainable programs. (pqac-00000008) | **No functional fabrication tests reported.** | Strong evidence that closed-loop agentic refinement improves executable CAD and geometric similarity. | Most direct methodological comparator to CADSmith. A valid comparison requires identical prompts, normalization, sampling, timeout, CadQuery/kernel version, execution metric, CD/IoU protocol, and ablations. Neither system’s reported geometric metrics establish grasp utility. |
| **Text2CAD-Bench** — Wang et al. (2026) | Benchmark for LLM-generated parametric CAD, emphasizing executability, geometry, and feature/design-intent understanding. | **600 examples / 1,200 prompts** across L1–L4; L3 references average **70.7 code lines** and **26.8 API calls**. Performance drops sharply on advanced topology; benchmark is single-turn and single-part. (pqac-00000009, pqac-00000010, pqac-00000015) | **No:** benchmark evaluation only. | Best available route to test whether a CAD agent generalizes beyond a private prompt set. | CADSmith’s 100% execution and 38× mean-CD improvement are not directly comparable until evaluated on the public benchmark under its prescribed zero-/few-shot conditions, including intent-level and IoU metrics—not only execution and CD. |
| **CME-CAD** | Generates CadQuery through heterogeneous collaborating experts and reinforcement learning. | Retrieved search evidence identifies a CADExpert benchmark and multi-expert RL, but provides no independently usable physical or end-effector result. | **No physical validation established.** | Relevant as a multi-agent architecture comparator. | Architecturally overlaps CADSmith’s multi-agent approach; a head-to-head needs matched model budgets, number of calls, wall-clock time, token cost, execution rate, geometric fidelity, editability, and constraint satisfaction. It does not close the physical-design loop. |
| **CAD-Recode** | Reverse-engineers executable Python CAD programs from point clouds rather than generating designs directly from textual functional requirements. | Produces interpretable code that can support subsequent LLM-based editing; the retrieved evidence supplies no end-effector or physical-test metric. (pqac-00000013, pqac-00000014) | **No task-level fabrication evidence established.** | Potential front end for converting scans of labware, legacy fingers, or fixtures into editable geometry. | Complementary rather than directly competitive: CADSmith starts from language and validates exact geometry/renders; CAD-Recode starts from observed shape. Neither demonstrates automatic functional redesign based on grasp outcomes. |
| **CADIR** | Defines a cross-backend editable intermediate representation for agentic CAD, including assemblies, constraints, configurations, and static collision checking. | Demonstrations include assemblies and planetary gears; dynamic and kinematic validation remain future work in the retrieved evidence. (pqac-00000011) | **No physical end-effector validation established.** | Relevant to multi-part grippers, tool changers, compliant inserts, and assembly-aware design—areas poorly represented by single-solid benchmarks. | CADSmith has stronger stated exact-kernel and render-judge validation; CADIR targets backend portability, explicit assemblies, and constraints. Combining these strengths would be more useful than comparing Chamfer Distance alone. |
| **DeepCAD** | Learns generative sequences of sketch-and-extrude CAD commands using a Transformer-style model. | Influential operation-sequence baseline, but command-sequence representations show worse validity and geometric accuracy than CadQuery on harder Text2CAD-Bench tasks. (pqac-00000009, pqac-00000010, pqac-00000014) | **No functional fabrication loop.** | Useful representation baseline for editable feature histories, but its restricted command vocabulary limits complex mechanisms and DfAM details. | CADSmith benefits from high-level CadQuery and pretrained code capabilities; comparison should include feature-history editability and constraint preservation, not just final meshes. |
| **Fusion 360 Gallery** | Dataset/environment containing human programmatic CAD-construction sequences. | Widely used for sequence-based CAD learning; retrieved evidence supplies no laboratory-gripper or physical-performance result. (pqac-00000011, pqac-00000013, pqac-00000014) | **No task-level physical tests.** | Useful training/evaluation corpus for feature-sequence generation and reconstruction. | It is a dataset, not an agent. CADSmith should use it only where representation conversion is fair and supplement it with functional labware-design tasks that Gallery does not measure. |
| **RealCADBench** | Evaluates parametric CAD generation from industrial design intents. | At the scan date, broader full-benchmark release/comparison was still prospective in the retrieved search record; no end-effector fabrication result was established. | **No physical validation established.** | Potentially valuable for testing industrial intent and complexity beyond primitive-centric prompts. | CADSmith should report on the finalized public split when available and avoid private-subset comparisons. RealCADBench still does not test fit, force, fatigue, manufacturability, or robot-task success. |
| **CADSmith** — in-house | Multi-agent text-to-CadQuery system with execution, exact OpenCASCADE measurements, three-view VLM judging, and iterative closed-loop refinement. | User-reported **100% execution rate** and **38× reduction in mean Chamfer Distance** versus zero-shot on a 100-prompt benchmark. | **Digital validation only so far; no reported autonomous physical design-test loop.** | Strong substrate for rapidly generating parametric fingers, nests, scoops, camera brackets, and tool interfaces with exact dimensional checks. | Must establish external validity through public benchmarks, released prompts/code, matched baselines and compute, confidence intervals, intent/constraint tests, human-expert comparisons, FDM printability, and—most importantly—physical grasp/seating/reliability outcomes. |
| **MATTERIX** — Darvish et al. | Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab digital-twin framework with USD assets, physics and semantics engines, perception, workflow planning, robot skills, and particle representations for liquids and powders. | Real-world demonstrations reported **75% pick-and-place** and **90% pouring** success. Powder weighing/scooping is represented, but cohesive adhesion, triboelectric charging, and quantitative powder fidelity were not validated. (pqac-00000016, pqac-00000018, pqac-00000020, pqac-00000021) | **Yes for robot workflows; no generated-gripper fabrication loop.** | Possible simulation and workstation substrate for collision, reachability, workflow, and coarse rigid/granular screening. | CADSmith generates geometry; MATTERIX evaluates environments and policies. Integration is promising, but MATTERIX cannot presently be treated as a validated oracle for cohesive AlSi10Mg/Si transfer or FDM contact mechanics. |
| **Robot-Aware Computational Design of Object-Specific Passive Grippers** — Omaisan (2026 preprint) | Screens object-specific passive grippers using contact zones, mechanism-family selection, robot insertion/collision sweeps, FEA, topology optimization, and watertight reconstruction. | Four object designs passed digital gates, but coupon calibration, physical fit/load/shake tests, and proposed 100-cycle tests were explicitly pending. (pqac-00000005, pqac-00000031) | **No:** simulation-only at publication stage. | Broadens computational design beyond grasp scoring by considering robot approach, retention, stress, and manufacturability. | More mechanics- and robot-aware than CADSmith’s current geometric/VLM validation, but lacks physical evidence and general language-to-CAD capability. It is a useful baseline architecture for adding engineering validators to CADSmith. |
| **Key unresolved absence** | A system accepts real labware geometry and functional requirements, generates editable manufacturable gripper CAD, prints it, tests it on a low-cost arm, measures grasp/seating/reliability, and feeds those measurements into redesign. | **No such fully closed, autonomous, real-SDL loop was identified.** Fit2Form and neural-physics co-design close important subsets; current CAD agents optimize digital similarity; MATTERIX simulates workflows; none combines all stages. (pqac-00000029, pqac-00000030, pqac-00000031, pqac-00000035) | **No.** | This is the clearest publishable intersection of CADSmith, rapid FDM iteration, PiPER, and materials-laboratory objects. | The opportunity is not merely “LLM designs a gripper”; it is demonstrating that physically informed, measured feedback produces statistically better task reliability than expert design, zero-shot CAD, geometry-only refinement, and simulation-only optimization. |


*Table: Comparison of generative CAD, gripper co-design, benchmarking, and digital-twin systems by quantitative evidence and physical validation. It identifies the central open gap: no published system autonomously closes the loop from laboratory-object requirements through editable CAD and fabrication to measured manipulation performance on a real SDL arm.*
